title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows, optimize cache & parallelism
author: Daniel Park
description:
Motivation: Our existing monolithic CI workflows have grown slow and brittle as we expanded lint, test, and release steps for multiple languages and packages. This causes long queue times, wasted cache uploads, and fragile release runs. This PR splits the large unified workflow into dedicated pipelines (lint, test, release) and improves caching/parallelism semantics to reduce runtime and improve developer feedback loops.

What changed: split workflows into three primary GitHub Actions workflows: .github/workflows/ci-lint.yml, .github/workflows/ci-test.yml, and .github/workflows/release.yml. Extracted common job templates to .github/workflows/templates/*.yml and consolidated reusable steps into scripts/ci/*.sh. Reworked cache keys to use environment-specific and matrix-aware keys to reduce unnecessary cache invalidation. Tuned job parallelism for test matrices and introduced the build-matrix cache restore step to reduce duplicate installs across matrix shards. Removed legacy bundled steps from the monorepo workflow and added targeted job-level conditions to avoid running release jobs on non-tag pushes.

Checklist: - [x] Split lint/test/release workflows and add templates - [x] Implement matrix-aware cache keys and restore/save steps - [x] Add lightweight smoke-tests for workflow changes - [x] Update developer docs (ci/README.md) - [x] Run on forked repo and validated against a set of representative PRs

Testing: Ran workflows on feature branches and a trial set of internal PRs (ENG-4321). Observed typical lint run time reduced by ~25% and test pipeline wall time reduced by ~30% due to better cache hits and parallelism. Release workflow tested in dry-run mode; genuine release jobs gated behind tag creation and required approvals. CI checks included unit, integration, lint, typecheck, and release-dryrun.

Rollback / Rollout plan: Merge to main during low-traffic window. Monitor CI queue and build times for 48 hours. If unexpected failures appear, revert by reverting the merge commit (squash). All changes are backward-compatible with current runners; templates are additive.

Related: follows patterns from previous CI hygiene work (see pr-104504 and pr-104516). Linear tickets: ENG-4321 (split workflows), ENG-4330 (optimize cache keys).

review_comments: Priya Shah: Nice decomposition. A few nits: can we make cache keys include matrix.os and node-version to avoid collisions across OS shards?
Author (Daniel Park): Good catch, updated cache-keys.sh to include matrix.os and runtime version token in the key generation (see commit f0d4a12).
Liam O'Connor: The release workflow needs a stricter condition so release jobs don't trigger on dependabot PRs. Suggest adding 'if: contains(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')' and an approval step.
Author (Daniel Park): Added tag-only guard and required 'release-approvers' CODEOWNERS entry; also added dry-run gate and annotated it in docs.
Evelyn Chen: The parallelism increase for python matrix looked good, but CI minutes budget may spike on larger runs. Could we add an hourly concurrency limit?
Author (Daniel Park): Added concurrency group to ci-test.yml and capped max-parallel at 6 for the heaviest matrix in the python jobs; noted tradeoffs in the PR description.
release_notes: Split CI workflows: lint/test/release; faster feedback loops and reduced wall time via matrix-aware cache keys; added templates for maintainability; updated docs in ci/README.md; release workflow now tag-gated and requires approvals; tuned test parallelism and concurrency caps.
